## T06 selector inventory

**Resolver and identity sources**

- [IdentityIndex::resolve / resolve_id / identifies](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/identity.rs:299) is the shared graph resolver. It parses a string as `PackageId`, then looks up qualified IDs by exact `(ecosystem, native name)` and bare IDs across registered native names; a bare name can resolve through a non-primary manifest. `identifies` resolves a parsed selector before comparing IDs. The current parser still accepts both slash and colon qualified forms, as specified by the current workspace contract.
- `PackageId::matches` and `resolve_unique` are separate model primitives at [identity.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs:161). The status helpers below call `resolve_unique`, not `IdentityIndex`.
- The producer for package IDs is workspace discovery and promotion in [walk.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:370). It also applies package configuration. Directory keys remain separate from printed IDs under accepted ADR 11.

**Exact selectors and glob patterns**

| Consumer | Current path and behavior |
|---|---|
| `[[package]]` rules | Parsed as `PackageId` in [config/resolve.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:571); matched in `walk.rs` via `rule_applies` at lines 392–395. Exact selector; ecosystem-prefixed rules are considered before bare rules, with declaration order within each pass. |
| `[[package-set]]` rules | Parsed as `PackagePattern` in [config/resolve.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:605); matched in [walk.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:383) and selected as fallback at lines 398–405. This is a glob language, with optional ecosystem scope, not an exact ID. Its parser and matcher are in [config/pattern.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/pattern.rs:23). |
| Fixed/linked group members | Raw strings resolve through `IdentityIndex::resolve` in [config/groups.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:140). Platform-manifest names are handled first at lines 158–172. These are exact references, not globs. |
| Changesets during version aggregation | Entries are parsed at [aggregate.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:295) and passed to `resolve_target_package`, which uses `resolve_id` at lines 168–186. Unknown and ambiguous cases follow separate paths. Exact references. |
| Changesets in status | `resolve_pending_changesets` parses and calls `PackageId::resolve_unique` at [commands/status.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs:36). `changeset_wellformedness_diagnostics` independently does so at lines 180–200. Both are exact parsed IDs but use the model primitive rather than the shared graph resolver. |
| `callisto add --package` | Splits severity from the final colon, resolves the name with `ws.identity.resolve`, and writes `resolved.display_name()` in [commands/add.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/add.rs:23). Exact reference; output is the package display ID. |
| Matrix `--package` | `resolve_selected_package` calls `identity.resolve` at [commands/matrix.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs:108). Exact reference. Matrix is named in T06 criteria but not its `modify` list. |
| Product/artifact package selectors | Release derivation resolves configured `PackageId`s using `identity.identifies` at [release/derive.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs:452) and related sites at 458, 491, and 622. Config parsing requires ecosystem-qualified values in [config/resolve.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:158). Exact references; outside T06’s listed modify files. |
| `pre.json` `initialVersions` | New keys are generated from display IDs by `initial_versions` and `pre_json_key` in [lib.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs:192). Existing keys are read and attributed in `assign_promoted_pre_keys` at lines 281–343; it first checks display IDs, then bare-name candidates and historical ownership. Exact keys, with historical ownership handling. |
| Default tags and prior tag history | Default tag names derive from display IDs in [model/tag.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/tag.rs:73). Tag lookup and previous-template lookup are in [tags.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs:146). Promoted-package fallback scans bare-name tag patterns and checks ownership at lines 176–190. Tag glob matching is a separate pattern operation. |
| Init output and reports | Text init output prints `package.id` in [commands/init.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/init.rs:275). Status report records are built from resolved pending entries; add emits the display ID. These are ID producers/readers rather than selector parsers. |

**T06 scope and evidence comparison**

T06 lists identity model/graph, walk, graph exports, config resolve/groups, aggregate, graph status, CLI add, the workspace/CLI/versioning specs, ADR 12, matrix, and matrix spec as modification scope. Its test list is only:

- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/identity_promotion_tests.rs`
- `crates/callisto-graph/tests/status_cascade_and_wellformedness_tests.rs`

The task text additionally calls for the commands `rtk cargo test -p callisto-model`, `rtk cargo test -p callisto-graph`, `rtk cargo test -p callisto-cli --test identity_promotion_tests`, and `rtk cargo test -p callisto-cli --test status_check_tests` in sequence. These were not run, per the read-only/no-Cargo instruction.

Named relevant tests found in the two listed test files include `promotion_keeps_the_last_tag_and_the_changelog`, `a_bare_changeset_name_after_promotion_says_how_to_qualify_it`, `a_pre_cycle_started_before_promotion_keeps_its_initial_version`, `display_id_is_bare_when_unique_and_qualified_when_promoted`, and status tests for unknown-package diagnostics, empty changesets, and unparseable changesets. Other directly relevant tests live outside T06’s listed test files: `identity.rs` has qualified/bare resolver tests; `config/resolve.rs` and `config/pattern.rs` cover rule resolution and glob scoping; `config/groups.rs` contains group resolution tests; `tags.rs` tests tag selection; status CLI tests are in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/status_check_tests.rs`. T06 specifically calls for a sibling `GroupTable::from_groups` regression, but that constructor/test file is not in T06’s file list.

**Contract and policy boundaries**

- Current [workspace spec](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/docs/specs/workspace.json:23) defines bare or slash-qualified display/selector IDs, accepts colon and slash forms for selectors and group members, and specifies bare-name ambiguity behavior. It also specifies the separate glob grammar for package sets.
- Current [CLI spec](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/docs/specs/cli.json:181) covers status diagnostics; add output and errors at lines 190–214; init’s qualified IDs at lines 217–234.
- Current [versioning spec](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/docs/specs/versioning.json:70) describes changeset resolution, and `VER-PRE-01` at line 152 describes display-ID baseline keys plus historical bare-key ownership.
- Accepted [ADR 11](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/docs/adr/0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md:11) remains current. [ADR 12](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/docs/adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md:1) is **Proposed** and explicitly leaves exact owner representation, legacy-record migration, wire-schema migration, and channel/private-registry policies unresolved. Its canonical slash-qualified references and rejection of new bare/colon aliases therefore are not current contract.

Unproven edges from this read-only inventory: whether every exact-selector consumer outside T06’s file list is intended to migrate; whether status’s two `resolve_unique` paths are to be replaced or retained; how the proposed compatibility boundary applies to old changesets, group/config entries, release decisions, and persisted pre-state; and which output/report schemas must change. Names and task scope alone do not settle those policies.
